refs.UpdateQuestionSetResponse$name: The updated or original name of the question set.

ResourceNotFoundException.base: The resource specified in the action doesn't exist.

SceneTrigger.base:
The perScene trigger, which runs the function once for each scene that a contextual metadata output reports. The function runs after the scene ends, with the media of that scene. To choose this trigger, set perScene to an empty object.

Specify contextualMetadataSettings to name the contextual metadata output that reports the scenes. You can't use this trigger with a function that references media.transcript or media.clip.

refs.Trigger$perScene: Run the function once for each scene boundary that a contextual metadata output reports. Requires contextualMetadataSettings. Can't be used with a function that references media.transcript or media.clip.

ScheduleAction.base: Describes one schedule action on a feed, including the changes it makes and whether it has run yet. Elemental Inference returns this structure in the ListScheduleActions operation.

ScheduleActionError.base: Describes the cause of a schedule action failure, including the failure type and a description of what went wrong.

refs.CreateScheduleActionResponse$error: A description of why the action failed. Elemental Inference returns this property only when the status is FAILED.
refs.ScheduleAction$error: A description of why the action failed. Elemental Inference returns this property only when the status is FAILED.

refs.ScheduleActionError$errorCode:
The type of failure. Valid values are the following:

INVALID_ACTION_TARGET

The action referred to something that didn't exist or wasn't valid at the scheduled time, for example an output that you deleted.

INTERNAL_ERROR

An unexpected error prevented the action from completing.

refs.ListScheduleActionsResponse$scheduleActi: A list of the schedule actions on the feed.

ScheduleActionOperation.base: Holds one typed configuration change that a schedule action makes to a feed. Each operation must contain exactly one property.

refs.CreateScheduleActionRequest$operations: Specifies the list of configuration changes that you want to make to the feed. Elemental Inference applies all the operations in an action together, in the order that you specify them. If any operation fails, Elemental Inference doesn't apply any of them.
refs.CreateScheduleActionResponse$operations: The configuration changes that the action makes to the feed.
refs.ScheduleAction$operations: The configuration changes that the action makes to the feed.

ScheduleActionStartConfiguration.base: Holds the typed start settings that determine when a schedule action runs. Currently, only fixed mode is supported.

refs.CreateScheduleActionResponse$status: The status of the action. After you create the action successfully, Elemental Inference sets the status to PENDING.
refs.ScheduleAction$status:
The status of the action. Valid values are the following:

PENDING

The action is waiting for its scheduled time.

COMPLETED

Elemental Inference applied all the action's operations to the feed.

FAILED

Elemental Inference couldn't apply the action.

SearchFilter.base: A filter for a fixture search. It is used in the filters array of a SearchFixtures request.

refs.SearchFixturesRequest$filters:
An array of filters that narrow the results. Each filter applies to one dimension of a fixture, such as the competitor. You can specify up to 10 filters.

A fixture must satisfy every filter in the array in order to appear in the results. Within one filter, a fixture must match at least one of the values.

refs.SearchFixturesRequest$maxResults:
The maximum number of fixtures to return for each API request.

The service might return fewer fixtures than the maxResults value. When more fixtures match the search, the response also includes a nextToken value that you can use to fetch the next batch of results.

ServiceQuotaExceededException.base: The request was rejected because it would exceed one or more service quotas for your account. Review your service quotas and either delete unused resources or request a quota increase.

ServiceUnavailableException.base: The service is temporarily unable to handle the request. Retry the request. If the problem persists, contact AWS Support.

ShotTrigger.base:
The perShot trigger, which runs the function once for each shot that Elemental Inference detects in the video. The function runs after the shot ends, with the media of that shot. To choose this trigger, set perShot to an empty object. The feed must have a video input.

You can't use this trigger with a function that references media.transcript or media.clip. If the function references media.contextual, specify contextualMetadataSettings.

refs.Trigger$perShot: Run the function once for each shot that Elemental Inference detects. Can't be used with a function that references media.transcript or media.clip.

refs.Competitor$name: The name of the competitor, as provided by the data source.
refs.FixtureSummary$name: The name of the fixture, as provided by the data source. For example, the names of the two competing teams.
refs.FixtureSummary$fixtureGroup: The group that the fixture belongs to, such as the competition, league, or tournament. The data source doesn't provide this information for every fixture.
refs.FixtureSummary$status: The status of the fixture in its lifecycle, as provided by the data source. For example, Scheduled or Completed.
refs.GetFixtureResponse$name: The name of the fixture, as provided by the data source. For example, the names of the two competing teams.
refs.GetFixtureResponse$fixtureGroup: The group that the fixture belongs to, such as the competition, league, or tournament. The data source doesn't provide this information for every fixture.
refs.GetFixtureResponse$status: The status of the fixture in its lifecycle, as provided by the data source. For example, Scheduled or Completed.
refs.ListDictionariesRequest$nextToken: The token that identifies the next batch of results to return.
refs.ListDictionariesResponse$nextToken: The token to use to retrieve the next batch of results.
refs.ListFeedsRequest$nextToken:
The token that identifies the batch of results that you want to see.

For example, you submit a ListFeeds request with MaxResults set at 5. The service returns the first batch of results (up to 5) and a NextToken value. To see the next batch of results, you can submit the ListFeeds request a second time and specify the NextToken value.
refs.ListFeedsResponse$nextToken: The token that identifies the batch of results that you want to see. For example, you submit a list request with MaxResults set at 5. The service returns the first batch of results (up to 5) and a NextToken value. To see the next batch of results, you can submit the list request a second time and specify the NextToken value.
refs.ListFunctionsRequest$nextToken: The token that identifies the page of results to return. Use the nextToken value from a previous response.
refs.ListFunctionsResponse$nextToken: The token to use in a subsequent request to get the next page of results. This field is absent when there are no more results.
refs.ListQuestionSetVersionsRequest$nextToken: The token that identifies the next batch of results to return.
refs.ListQuestionSetVersionsResponse$nextToke: The token to use to retrieve the next batch of results.
refs.ListQuestionSetsRequest$nextToken: The token that identifies the next batch of results to return.
refs.ListQuestionSetsResponse$nextToken: The token to use to retrieve the next batch of results.
refs.ListScheduleActionsRequest$nextToken: The token that identifies the batch of results that you want to see. To see the next batch, submit the request a second time and specify the NextToken value that Elemental Inference returned.
refs.ListScheduleActionsResponse$nextToken: The token that identifies the next batch of results. Elemental Inference returns it only when more results are available.
refs.SearchFixturesRequest$nextToken:
The token that identifies the batch of results that you want to see.

For example, you submit a SearchFixtures request with maxResults set at 5. The service returns the first batch of results (up to 5) and a nextToken value. To see the next batch of results, you submit the SearchFixtures request a second time, with the same search criteria, and specify the nextToken value.
refs.SearchFixturesResponse$nextToken:
The token that identifies the next batch of results. To see the next batch, submit the SearchFixtures request again, with the same search criteria, and specify this value in nextToken.

This parameter is absent when there are no more results to return.

refs.CreateFeedResponse$dataEndpoints: An array of endpoints for the feed. Typically, there is only one endpoint. The feed receives source media at this endpoint (when the calling application calls PutMedia) and returns the resulting metadata to this endpoint (when the calling application calls GetMetadata).

SubtitlingConfig.base: A type of OutputConfig, used when the output in a feed is for the smart subtitling feature. Smart subtitling uses automatic speech recognition (ASR) to generate live TTML subtitles from the audio in your source media.

refs.OutputConfig$subtitling: The output config type that applies to the smart subtitling feature.

SubtitlingSettings.base:
The smart subtitles output on this feed that a function reads media.transcript from. Specify this structure for a function that references media.transcript. That function must use a fixedInterval trigger.

If the function output is ENABLED, the output that you name must also be ENABLED.

refs.FunctionConfig$subtitlingSettings: The smart subtitles output on this feed to read the transcript from. Required for a function that references media.transcript.

refs.ContextualMetadataConfig$summaryGenerati:
Specifies whether Elemental Inference generates a descriptive summary of the media content for this output, along with the objects and actions that it detects. This setting is independent of extendedAnalysis.

Valid values:

  • ENABLED (default) – Elemental Inference populates the summary, objects, and actions fields, along with the IAB taxonomy and GARM suitability classifications.

  • DISABLED – Elemental Inference doesn't populate the summary, objects, and actions fields.

refs.FixtureSummary$scheduledStart: The scheduled start time of the fixture, as provided by the data source. The actual start time might differ.
refs.GetFixtureResponse$scheduledStart: The scheduled start time of the fixture, as provided by the data source. The actual start time might differ.

refs.UntagResourceRequest$tagKeys: The keys of the tags to delete.

refs.CreateDictionaryRequest$tags: Optional tags to associate with the dictionary.
refs.CreateDictionaryResponse$tags: Any tags that you included when you created the dictionary.
refs.CreateFeedRequest$tags: Optional tags. You can also add tags later, using TagResource.
refs.CreateFeedResponse$tags: Any tags that you included when you created the feed.
refs.CreateFunctionRequest$tags: The tags to associate with this function.
refs.CreateQuestionSetRequest$tags: Optional tags to associate with the question set. You can also add tags later, using TagResource.
refs.CreateQuestionSetResponse$tags: Any tags that you included when you created the question set.
refs.CreateQuestionSetVersionResponse$tags: Any tags associated with the question set.
refs.GetFeedResponse$tags: A list of the tags, if any, for the feed.
refs.GetQuestionSetResponse$tags: The tags associated with the question set.
refs.ListTagsForResourceResponse$tags: A list of the tags that belong to this resource.
refs.TagResourceRequest$tags: A list of tags to add to the resource.
refs.UpdateQuestionSetResponse$tags: Any tags associated with the question set.

TemplateGroup.base: A named set of graphics-compositing templates used by the crop feature, specified in the templateGroups array of a CroppingConfig.

refs.CroppingConfig$templateGroups: An array of template groups for the crop output. Each template group provides the graphics-compositing templates that Elemental Inference applies to the cropped video. You can specify from 1 to 4 template groups.

refs.TemplateGroup$templateUris: An array of Amazon S3 URIs that point to the graphics-compositing templates for this group. You can specify 1 or 2 URIs. Each URI must be in the form s3://bucket-name/key. Elemental Inference reads these templates using the IAM role that you specify in accessRoleArn.

refs.FixedModeScheduleActionStartSettings$sch:
The UTC time at which the action runs. Specify the time in whole seconds. For the range of times that you can specify, see the AWS Elemental Inference User Guide.

This time is approximate. The change can take a few minutes to take effect on the media that the feed is processing.
refs.QuestionSetVersionSummary$lastModifiedAt: For DRAFT, the time when you created the question set or last updated DRAFT. For a published version, the time when you published it.

TooManyRequestException.base: The request was denied due to request throttling. Too many requests have been made within a given time period. Reduce the frequency of requests and use exponential backoff when retrying.

refs.SubtitlingConfig$language:
The language of the audio in the source media. Elemental Inference uses this setting to optimize transcription accuracy. Specify the language using an ISO 639-2/T three-letter code, optionally with a region subtag. Supported values:

  • eng – English

  • eng-au – English (Australia)

  • eng-gb – English (United Kingdom)

  • eng-us – English (United States)

  • fra – French

  • ita – Italian

  • deu – German

  • spa – Spanish

  • por – Portuguese

  • ara – Arabic

Trigger.base: Determines when a function runs. Specify exactly one member.

UpdateClippingDataSourceConfiguration.base: Attaches a game to an event clipping output at the action's scheduled time. This is a type of ScheduleActionOperation, and the output must be an event clipping output.

refs.ScheduleActionOperation$updateClippingDa: The operation type that attaches a game to an event clipping output.

refs.UpdateFunctionRequest$requestExpression: A new request expression for the function. Elemental Inference derives contextTypes again from the new expression. While a feed references the function, the new expression must reference the same media context as the current one.

refs.UpdateFunctionResponse$requestExpression: The JSONata expression that builds the request. Elemental Inference evaluates it against the media object of the feed, which holds the media and metadata that the function asked for.

UpdateOutput.base: Contains configuration information about one output in a feed. It is used in the UpdateFeed action.

refs.UpdateFeedRequest$outputs: Required. You can specify the existing array of outputs (to leave outputs unchanged) or you can specify a new array.

UpdateOutputStatus.base: Enables or disables an output at the action's scheduled time. This is a type of ScheduleActionOperation.

refs.ScheduleActionOperation$updateOutputStat: The operation type that enables or disables an output.

ValidationException.base: The input fails to satisfy the constraints specified by the service. Check the error message for details about which parameter or field is invalid and correct the request before retrying.

YesNoPerOptionOptionList.base: An array of the options of a yesNoPerOption question.

refs.YesNoPerOptionQuestion$options: The options that you ask the question about. You can specify from 1 to 50 options. Each option counts as one item toward the limit of 100 scored items in a version.

YesNoPerOptionQuestion.base: A question that you ask Elemental Inference separately about each of its options. Elemental Inference answers yes or no for each option. Word the question so that it fits any of the options. For example, ask Is this overlay visible? with one option for each overlay. You specify it in the yesNoPerOption array of a question set.

refs.CreateQuestionSetRequest$yesNoPerOption: An array of questions that you ask about each of their options. Elemental Inference answers yes or no for each option. You can specify up to 10 yesNoPerOption questions. An empty array is the same as omitting this property.
refs.CreateQuestionSetResponse$yesNoPerOption: The yesNoPerOption questions that you specified in the request, in the order that you specified them. Elemental Inference doesn't return this property if the request didn't include any yesNoPerOption questions.
refs.CreateQuestionSetVersionResponse$yesNoPe: The yesNoPerOption questions in this version. Elemental Inference doesn't return this property if the version has no yesNoPerOption questions.
refs.GetQuestionSetResponse$yesNoPerOption: The yesNoPerOption questions in this version. Elemental Inference doesn't return this property if the version has no yesNoPerOption questions.
refs.UpdateQuestionSetRequest$yesNoPerOption: An array of questions that you ask about each of their options, to replace all the yesNoPerOption questions in DRAFT. You can specify up to 10 yesNoPerOption questions. If not specified, the yesNoPerOption questions are not changed. To remove all the yesNoPerOption questions, specify an empty array.
refs.UpdateQuestionSetResponse$yesNoPerOption: The yesNoPerOption questions in this version. Elemental Inference doesn't return this property if the version has no yesNoPerOption questions.

YesNoQuestion.base: A question that you ask Elemental Inference, which answers with yes or no. You specify it in the yesNo array of a question set.

refs.CreateQuestionSetRequest$yesNo: An array of questions that Elemental Inference answers with yes or no. You can specify up to 50 yesNo questions. An empty array is the same as omitting this property.
refs.CreateQuestionSetResponse$yesNo: The yesNo questions that you specified in the request, in the order that you specified them. Elemental Inference doesn't return this property if the request didn't include any yesNo questions.
refs.CreateQuestionSetVersionResponse$yesNo: The yesNo questions in this version. Elemental Inference doesn't return this property if the version has no yesNo questions.
refs.GetQuestionSetResponse$yesNo: The yesNo questions in this version. Elemental Inference doesn't return this property if the version has no yesNo questions.
refs.UpdateQuestionSetRequest$yesNo: An array of questions that Elemental Inference answers with yes or no, to replace all the yesNo questions in DRAFT. You can specify up to 50 yesNo questions. If not specified, the yesNo questions are not changed. To remove all the yesNo questions, specify an empty array.
refs.UpdateQuestionSetResponse$yesNo: The yesNo questions in this version. Elemental Inference doesn't return this property if the version has no yesNo questions.
